title: feat(scripts): sync docs image tags at version time so check:docs-image-tag cannot misfire
body:
Fixes #9064

`check:docs-image-tag` (#9018) pins the docs' concrete image and CLI tags to `packages/cli`'s version, so a version bump reddens it until the doc surfaces move in the same change. That is the mechanism. The defect was **where the red landed**: never on the change that caused it.

Adds `scripts/sync-docs-image-tags.mjs` to the root `version` chain, beside the two sync scripts already there — the shape this repo already chose for the identical drift class (`sync-template-versions.mjs`, #2907). The gate stays exactly as it was: the backstop. The rewriter makes the correct state automatic.

## Re-derived, not copied

Every fact in the card was re-verified on the merged ref (`origin/main` at `4e3a4c3c8`):

| Claim | Verdict |
|:---|:---|
| Root `version` = `changeset version && sync-protocol-version && sync-template-versions` | **Exact**, verbatim |
| Neither sync script touches a doc surface | **Confirmed** — grep for `Dockerfile\|content/docs\|docker/README\|ghcr` over both returns zero hits |
| `sync-template-versions.mjs` header: release PRs opened by changesets/action with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger CI | **Confirmed**, quoted verbatim in the new script's header |
| `check-docs-image-tag.mjs` exports `SURFACES` / `PATTERNS` / `extractOccurrences` | **Confirmed** — all three present |

## One difference from the card's plan, reported not reconciled

⚠️ The card and triage both assumed the rewriter could simply `import` those exports. **It could not.** `check-docs-image-tag.mjs` had no entry-point guard, so importing it *ran the gate and called `process.exit()`* — measured: a probe importing `SURFACES` never reached its own next line. The failure would also have been silent in the worst way, since the exit code was the corpus's verdict: an importer looks fine while the corpus is green and dies with an unrelated exit 1 the day a pin goes stale.

So this PR adds the guard (the repo's own idiom, stated with the same rationale in `check-adr-links`, `check-doc-anchors`, `check-kernel-hook-pairs`) and exports `VERSION_SOURCE`. Both are **additive**: nothing about what the gate asserts changes, and both `check:docs-image-tag` invocations run the file directly, where the branch is taken exactly as before. Verified — same `OK` line, same 44 self-test assertions, before and after.

## Why the lists are imported

`SURFACES`, `PATTERNS`, `VERSION_SOURCE`, the concreteness classifier, the extractor **and the verdict** all come from the gate. The rewrite is defined as "make the gate's own findings go away", and the final verdict is literally `checkSurfaces()` — so the rewriter and the gate cannot drift apart by construction. Two independent surface lists would reproduce this very defect one layer up.

## The end-to-end claim, on the real corpus

Bumped `packages/cli` 17.0.0 to 17.1.0 in the worktree, exactly as `changeset version` would:

```
STEP 2 — gate WITHOUT the rewriter (today's release PR):
  check-docs-image-tag: 8 problem(s) -- 8 STALE            exit=1

STEP 3 — the rewriter (what the version script now runs):
  docker/README.md                          32:6, 43:3 image-tag · 65:45 build-arg
  content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx  76:3, 94:3, 145:6 image-tag · 163:20 npm-pin
  content/docs/upgrading.mdx                41:8 image-tag
  8 pin(s) across 3 surface(s) -> 17.1.0                   exit=0

STEP 4 — gate on the same tree:
  check-docs-image-tag: OK (3/3 surfaces, 8 pins vs 17.1.0)  exit=0
```

`git diff` after the rewrite: **9 changed lines — the 8 pins and the version bump itself.** The tag-table metavariable rows, rolling tags and prose were untouched. Tree restored afterwards; the branch carries no doc edits.

## Proving the rewriter can fail (both directions)

An inert rewriter and an over-eager one are equally fatal, and a green corpus distinguishes neither — there is nothing for a correct rewriter to do to it. `--self-test` carries 35 assertions over temp fixtures on the real `syncSurfaces` path, with a control per limb. Three ablations, each reverted:

| Ablation | Result |
|:---|:---|
| **Inert** — `rewriteText` returns no rewrites | RED, 9 named failures, incl. `after the rewrite the gate reports ZERO findings — got ["STALE@4",…]` |
| **Over-eager** — drop the concreteness filter | RED, 7 failures. Byte-identity control named the exact corruption: `latest -> 17.0.0`, `17.0 -> 17.0.0`, `17 -> 17.0.0` |
| **Left-to-right splice** instead of right-to-left | RED — and *earlier than predicted*: the offset-integrity guard refused to splice rather than corrupting the line |

The over-eager control is the load-bearing one: a clean corpus must be left **byte-identical and unwritten** (mtime asserted too). Rolling tags, the tag-table metavariable, the placeholder in Dockerfile header comments, `${OS_CLI_VERSION}` interpolations and version-shaped historical prose ("removed in @objectstack/spec 16.4.2") are all asserted unmoved.

The self-test was hardened mid-run: the inert ablation first died of a `TypeError` two limbs before the byte-identity control ran, so an empty result set is now *named* instead of crashing.

## Boundary

⛔ Version-time **sync step only**. No `changeset publish`, no tagging, no Version Packages PR, no workflow invocation. Release execution stays human (#6170, Prime Directive #15). It is reached only because `changesets/action` runs `pnpm run version` on release.yml's `version-pr` lane, which carries no `publish:` input and is structurally unable to publish. Being *on* the release path is not performing a release — the distinction the PM drew in the dispatch comment.

## CI wiring

New `check:docs-image-tag-sync` step in lint.yml's ESLint job, next to the gate. Only the `--self-test` runs there, deliberately: the rewriter has nothing to do on a green corpus, so CI can never observe it working — the self-test is the only place it is observed both working and failing. Same job as the gate, since they share one surface list. `check:required-contexts` stays green (job name, matrix and continue-on-error all unchanged).

## Verification

Gate union re-derived from the **final** diff with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (which discovered the new family itself) and run at `cf19396d8` = `git rev-parse --short HEAD`:

```
check:docs-image-tag                PASS   check:type-check-coverage        PASS
check:docs-image-tag-sync           PASS   check:type-check-debt            PASS *
check:node-version                  PASS   check:workflow-status-functions  PASS
check:required-contexts             PASS   check:nul-bytes                  PASS
check:shard-attestation             PASS   check-shard-attestation.mjs      PASS
```

`*` `check:type-check-debt` first failed on its **build-closure precondition** in the fresh worktree ("55 workspace dependencies have no built type entry point on disk"), not on any assertion. Built the closure (`turbo run build`, 70 tasks, under the shared verification lock) and re-ran: OK, 33 ledger entries re-measured, none above its recorded number. ESLint clean on both scripts.

`skip-changeset`: `scripts/`, the private root manifest (`@objectstack/spec-monorepo`) and a workflow are not published package source, so this PR releases nothing.
